name: Rocket from the Crypt
label: Headhunter
lede: Six people in matching outfits, a game show wheel for a setlist, and a promise of free shows for life if you tattooed the logo on your body.

eras.title: Out of the ashes of Pitchfork
eras.text: John Reis pulls a new band out of the wreckage of his old one, gives everybody a stage name, and puts them in matching outfits before the first record is even out. The horns arrive almost immediately.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: John Reis
years.h: Pitchfork ends. Reis starts Rocket from the Crypt
years.p: John Reis, now "Speedo", takes the name from the defunct 1970s punk band [[Rocket from the Tombs|3ce68b60-1c6c-4b0f-87fd-0f13410df01d]]. The first line-up lasts about six months.
years.xp:
Reis had formed Pitchfork at 17 with [[Rick Froberg|07d99b38-fa92-4916-a190-1240b1d2e402]] and played guitar until it dissolved in 1990. He and Froberg went straight on to [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]], while Reis started Rocket from the Crypt on the side.

The first line-up was Reis, guitarist Andy Stamets, bassist Pete Reichert, a drummer named Sean and backing vocalist Elaina. Sean and Elaina both left San Diego within months.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Paint as a Fragrance · Headhunter HED #003
years.p: The first album, cut by the short-lived original line-up and put out by San Diego's Headhunter label. Trouser Press was not kind about the sleeve.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Atom Willard arrives, Apollo 9 blows sax, everyone gets a new name
years.p: Drummer Adam Willard becomes "Atom", Stamets becomes "ND", Reichert becomes "Petey X", and Paul O'Beirne joins on sax as "Apollo 9".
years.xp:
The band dressed alike and borrowed from 1950s to 1970s garage, rock and soul acts. Encyclopedia.com says Reis added the sax after hearing Stax 45s.

They also made their own lyric booklets and handed out noisemakers, which is where the show-band reputation starts.

eras.title: Riots, rockets and a major-label handshake
eras.text: A record made in Los Angeles while the city burns, a fanzine offer that turns fans into walking billboards, and a deal with Interscope that Reis makes sure leaves the vinyl door open.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography
years.h: Circa: Now! · Headhunter HED #015
years.p: Recorded in Los Angeles during the Rodney King riots. "Sturdy Wrists" and "Ditch Digger" get the videos.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com places the sessions in Los Angeles in 1992, during the riots that followed the Rodney King verdict. The album came out on Headhunter first and was picked up by Interscope and Atlantic in 1993.

years.cap: The rocket. Permanent, and it gets you in free.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · ABC News: Rocket From the Crypt Takes Off · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Free Rocket From the Crypt tattoos
years.h: Get the rocket tattooed, never pay to see the band again
years.p: John Reis announces in a fanzine that anyone with a Rocket from the Crypt tattoo gets into every show free, for life.
years.xp:
That is the Wikipedia telling. Reis has since told a different version: in an ABC News piece from 2001 he said the practice started when friends of the band got tattooed and were added to guest lists, and that it was "perpetuated by people who were into us, not by us preaching this gospel of tattoos". ABC put the total at over 3,000 people, about 450 of them in San Diego, and noted the free admission occasionally strains a venue's finances.

MTV VJ Kennedy showed her band tattoo on national television during the band's Interscope years. The policy was still running in 2019, when tattooer Maggiore set up free flash at the Halloween show, and a Pushead-designed logo was the best seller.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Interscope signs Rocket from the Crypt and Drive Like Jehu
years.p: Reis takes both bands to the label in one go, with the right to keep putting out vinyl elsewhere.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the deal was struck in 1992 and Encyclopedia.com says the end of 1992. Either way it meant Reis's two bands, one a horn-driven show band and the other a fractured post-hardcore four-piece, were label-mates.

The carve-out for vinyl on other labels is why the next few years are full of small-label singles and EPs.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Trumpeter JC 2000 joins, and MTV plays "Ditch Digger"
years.p: Jason Crane completes the horn section. The dates for his arrival vary between sources.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Six months off while Reis makes Yank Crime with Drive Like Jehu
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt takes a break while Reis records Drive Like Jehu's second album, released by Cargo, Interscope and Atlantic.

eras.title: The free tour and the top of the pops
eras.text: Tickets are free, the setlist is picked by a game show wheel, and a single called "On a Rope" gets the band onto Top of the Pops. Then the follow-up lands on a label that has moved on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Hot Charity · nine songs, and the tour is free
years.p: Reis puts the record out on Perfect Sound and takes the band on a six-week tour with no admission charged, funded by Interscope.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com says the vinyl run was 5,000 copies. It followed the two-track The State of Art Is on Fire EP, a vinyl-only release on Sympathy for the Record Industry that April.

The Interscope-backed free tour is described by Wikipedia as running six weeks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scream, Dracula, Scream! · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Scream, Dracula, Scream! · the one with the strings
years.p: Reis produces it himself. The basic tracks go down live on a 4-track machine in about two months.
years.xp:
Videos were shot for "On a Rope", "Born in '69" and "Young Livers". Wikipedia notes the record was built on a bigger budget with string sections.

Reis later had mixed feelings about the strings:

"Conceptually it was a great idea but I didn't really think it was working." (Reis, via Wikipedia)

years.cap: The uniform, the horns and the wheel.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: A game show wheel picks the setlist
years.p: Shows come with raffles, fire breathing and matching outfits, and the band spins a wheel to decide what to play next.

years.cap: "On a Rope" gets Rocket from the Crypt onto British TV.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Scream, Dracula, Scream!
years.h: "On a Rope" goes to No. 12 and the band goes on Top of the Pops
years.p: The single enters the UK chart at No. 12, and the band wins the Phillip Hall Radar award at the NME Awards.
years.xp:
An American punk band with six matching outfits and a sax player was suddenly on MTV Europe and Top of the Pops. The band also toured the US, UK and Europe, supporting Rancid and Soundgarden and headlining their own dates.

Fans who had the rocket tattoo were being shown on TV too: MTV's Kennedy displayed hers on air.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: RFTC · Kevin Shirley produces, Interscope loses interest
years.p: "Break It Up" and "Lipstick" get radio play, but sales disappoint and the label turns to bigger acts.
years.xp: Wikipedia says album sales underperformed and Interscope shifted focus to bigger sellers; the San Diego Reader says the label ignored the band. Chris Prescott of Tanner and No Knife toured with the band on percussion and keyboards.

eras.title: Cut carefully, play loud, leave on Halloween
eras.text: Drummer Atom quits, the Interscope years end, and Reis builds a life around Hot Snakes, Sultans and his own label. Rocket from the Crypt becomes a band he plays when he wants to, until he decides he doesn't.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: John Reis
years.h: Cut Carefully and Play Loud EP · Flapping Jet
years.p: A stopgap EP that lands the same year SLAMM magazine names them the best San Diego band of all time.
years.xp: The San Diego label Swami, Reis's own imprint, put out the rarities collection All Systems Go 2 that October. Wikipedia lists Reis's new bands Hot Snakes and Sultans as starting around the same time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Atom Willard leaves, and Interscope is over
years.p: The drummer exits after disagreements about the band's direction. Willard goes on to Weezer's crew, then the Offspring and Angels & Airwaves.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · ABC News: Rocket From the Crypt Takes Off
years.h: Group Sounds · Vagrant, with a skateboarder on drums
years.p: Superchunk's Jon Wurster fills in on the early sessions before pro skater Mario Rubalcaba takes the stool as "Ruby Mars".
years.xp: Rocket from the Crypt had not toured for two and a half years when they set out to promote it. ABC News reported two shows a day for the first two weeks, with daytime free sets at record stores.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Magnet: Rocket From The Crypt, Speedo's Army
years.h: Live from Camp X-Ray · the last studio album
years.p: Reis calls it "a fairly mundane punk record".

years.cap: The last night, at the Westin in downtown San Diego.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Magnet: Rocket From The Crypt, Speedo's Army · Wikipedia: R.I.P. (Rocket from the Crypt album) · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: The farewell: Reis enters on a gurney, leaves as a witch doctor
years.p: Twenty-five songs, host El Vez, and a capacity crowd at the Westin ballroom on Halloween 2005.
years.xp:
Reis's official reason was a joke: the band was disbanding "in protest of illegal music downloading". His real one, per Wikipedia, was that he could no longer sustain the "strenuous, military-like" practice the band demanded and anything less would be a different band.

The show was filmed. Encyclopedia.com places it at the Casbah, but Wikipedia and Magnet both say the Westin.

eras.title: Buried, sort of
eras.text: The band is dead, but the DVD, the compilations and a children's TV show keep it moving. Reis has other plans.

years.src: Wikipedia: R.I.P. (Rocket from the Crypt album) · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography
years.h: R.I.P. · the farewell show, on CD and DVD
years.p: Vagrant releases it two years after a rough cut circulated on Swami.
years.xp: A rough cut, RFTC 10/31/05, came out on Swami in October 2006. A fire at the video production company Fourth Project delayed the final version. Pitchfork rated it 7.6.

years.src: Wikipedia: John Reis · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Reis moves on with the Night Marchers
years.p: His new band's first album, See You in Magic, comes out in April 2008.
years.xp:
Reis had played in Sultans until the band broke up in January 2007. Petey X started Merch Lackey. Apollo 9 teaches project management and marketing at a San Diego high school. JC 2000 moved to Belize. Ruby Mars co-owns Thirsty Moon Records.

Reis said in May 2008: "I do have a little regret in that now that we don't play together I don't see those guys anymore."

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Punknews: Rocket from the Crypt, He's a Chef
yt: "He's a Chef" on Yo Gabba Gabba
years.h: Rocket from the Crypt appear on Yo Gabba Gabba!
years.p: With Atom Willard back on drums, they perform "He's a Chef", released only through Volcom stores.

years.big: "I thought that was it and I never wanted to play those fucking songs ever again."
years.src: LA Record: Rocket from the Crypt, Yes to Everything · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: The reunion is on, after all
years.p: Reis to the LA Record in 2014, on why the December 2012 announcement was a surprise.
years.xp: Fan demand changed his mind. Continuing to say no "seemed ridiculous" when people wanted to see them, he said, and he kept the plan loose: "This could end after these shows or it could go on."

eras.title: Back from the crypt
eras.text: Annual Halloween shows, a stack of festival slots and a back catalogue that keeps coming out of the vault.

years.src: San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt · setlist.fm: Rocket From the Crypt at Riot Fest Chicago 2013
years.h: Riot Fest Chicago: the first big-stage show back
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt play Humboldt Park during the reunion's first year back.
years.xp: The band also played a House of Blues Halloween show that October 31, starting the annual Halloween tradition that continues to this day.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Vintage Piss: the record made with Sonny Vincent and left unmixed for 12 years
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt backed Vincent on the original 2003 sessions. Reis finally finished and produced it after the reunion.

years.src: San Diego Reader: Free Rocket From the Crypt tattoos
years.h: Free flash tattoos at the Halloween show
years.p: Tattooer Maggiore, who tattooed Reis backstage in Milan in 2018, does free rocket tattoos before the set.
years.xp: She got through eight flashes in about two and a half hours. The Pushead-designed logo was the best seller, and the San Diego Reader says the Halloween free tattoos have become an annual thing.

years.src: San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Riot Fest: Group Sounds, front to back
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt play the whole 2001 album in Chicago.

years.h: Lost masters and the Scream, Frankenstein, Scream! tour
years.p: Loudwire's headline says the band found lost masters online and announced tour dates.
